extraction.name: NeedleBench
extraction.description: A comprehensive synthetic bilingual long-context benchmark/framework for evaluating LLM retrieval and reasoning across information-sparse and information-dense tasks with adaptive context lengths, including the Ancestral Trace Challenge.
extraction.creator: Mo Li; Songyang Zhang; Taolin Zhang; Haodong Duan; Yunxin Liu; Kai Chen
extraction.citeAs: Li, M., Zhang, S., Zhang, T., Duan, H., Liu, Y., & Chen, K. (2025). NeedleBench: Evaluating LLM Retrieval and Reasoning Across Varying Information Densities. Transactions on Machine Learning Research. Reviewed on OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=cEvmIKsRw0
extraction.rai:dataCollection: NeedleBench is programmatically constructed using largely synthetic needles and generated ATC instances, with English filler text from PaulGrahamEssays and Chinese filler text from ChineseDomainModelingEval. ATC instances are generated algorithmically by sampling unique names, assigning relationship terms and templates, shuffling statements, and creating prompts and answers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Synthetic, abstract, fictional statements and relational facts are used as needles; filler/haystack text comes from the PaulGrahamEssays dataset for English and the ChineseDomainModelingEval dataset for Chinese.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For information-sparse tasks, key data points are strategically inserted at various depths in long contexts; ATC relationship statements are randomly shuffled to eliminate positional bias; a context-length buffer is subtracted to avoid instruction truncation across tokenizers.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Token lengths are measured using the GPT-4 tokenizer, and a buffer is subtracted from target context length to mitigate instruction truncation caused by tokenizer discrepancies across models.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Ground-truth labels/answers are generated automatically from predefined synthetic facts and the constructed family structure. Evaluation uses predefined core keywords for retrieval tasks and exact-match on answers in \boxed{...} format for reasoning tasks. Additionally, approximately 10% of ATC errors were manually annotated for error analysis.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors manually annotated about 10% of ATC errors and categorized them into under-thinking, partial understanding, instruction following, repetitive output, hallucination, and other errors. They also analyzed output-format compliance and false error rates for small models.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: All reproducible scripts, code, and datasets will be made available upon publication; all codes and resources are publicly available at OpenCompass.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Language (English and Chinese); synthetic names and familial relationships are included, with notes that gender consistency of names should be ignored.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to provide critical insights and targeted evaluation tools for understanding and improving long-context capabilities of LLMs, especially for real-world applications such as legal document retrieval, academic research, and business intelligence.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Realistic benchmarks may suffer from data contamination and memorization due to overlap with pretraining data; NeedleBench uses synthetic tasks to mitigate this. The benchmark also notes cross-lingual performance gaps between English and Chinese and addresses positional bias by shuffling ATC statements.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Because NeedleBench is synthetic, it may not fully reflect the complexity of real-world tasks. The paper also notes that realistic benchmarks may be saturated and confounded by memorization, while current models still struggle with integrating scattered evidence in long contexts.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation/benchmarking of LLM long-context retrieval and reasoning, including bilingual assessment across information-sparse and information-dense tasks and adaptive context lengths.

name.evidence: To address these limitations, we introduce NeedleBench, a comprehensive synthetic framework designed to assess retrieval and reasoning performance in bilingual long-context tasks with adaptive context lengths

description.evidence: To address the limitations of existing long-context evaluation methods, we present NeedleBench, a dataset framework that encompasses both information-sparse and information-dense tasks. NeedleBench is designed to provide a comprehensive, targeted assessment of models’ abilities to extract, analyze, and reason over long texts.
